text:
Alice M.: quick brain dump — we need to pick sane defaults for proxy lease revokes + client hints. current chaos: short TTLs -> flapping failovers, long TTLs -> stale-residency writes. thoughts?
Ben I.: can we separate control-plane lease window from client-facing hint TTL? keep control-plane shortish (30s) and hints longer (5m)?
Carol R.: +1 to separation. but long client hints mean clients may keep sending to wrong region for minutes. how do we do graceful rebind?
Dan (runtime): runtime idea: attach an "X-Region-Preference" header with (region, expires_at, epoch). proxies can honor or ask control-plane to validate on mismatch. cheap validity check = hash(epoch, tenant).
Alice M.: example header we talked about earlier:
```
X-Region-Preference: us-west-2;expires=1717428200;epoch=42
```
Ben I.: that helps. if proxy sees mismatch and expires < now -> contact control-plane fallback; if control-plane says revoked -> proxy returns 409-ish instructing client to retry with new hint.
Carol R.: 409 might break some SDKs. can we do 307 redirect with a small JSON body explaining new region? SDKs can auto-follow.
Eve (security): redirects for writes feel odd for compliance — we must surface reason and signed proof that new region is allowed for tenant. otherwise audit gets messy.
Dan (runtime): signed proof = control-plane signs a short-lived token included in redirect Location or in header. token includes tenant id, allowed region, expiry, and a signature. proxies verify via public key cache.
Alice M.: tradeoffs: token approach = extra crypto and key rotation complexity, but clear audit trail and safe. alternative = proxy-to-control-plane mutual TLS check on every mismatch -> more load.
Ben I.: load can be mitigated by caching signed tokens at proxy until expiry. control-plane issues tokens when ownership changes. cache invalidation via pubsub to region proxies for fast revokes.
Carol R.: what about client-side behavior? SDKs should refresh region hint on 307 or on explicit header. small retry loop: 1 immediate redirect, then backoff 200ms if second attempt 422/locked. docs + tests needed.
Alice M.: agree. propose defaults: control-plane lease TTL = 60s, proxy hint TTL = 300s, token expiry = 30s, and on-lease-revoke push invalidation via control-plane pubsub. anyone strongly opposed?
Eve (security): token expiry 30s ok. need KMS-based signing + rotation plan. add audit log entry for every revoke + token issue.
Dan (runtime): runtime notes: implement public-key cache refresh every 5s, and fall back to mTLS check if signature missing. batch validation RPC to control-plane to reduce QPS.
Ben I.: ops-bot: deploying a small canary to exercise the flow would help.
ops-bot: deploy status: canary/lease-proxy-flow -> started 1717429000; 3/3 green for proxy, control-plane auth still staging.
Carol R.: follow-up items: 1) RFC snippet for header + token format, 2) SDK retry semantics doc, 3) control-plane pubsub invalidation api, 4) test harness for rapid revoke. I'll draft the RFC.
Alice M.: thx. Carol, please include example traces (happy path + revoke) and a small perf sketch (token checks per second at 1k tenants).
Ben I.: I'll prototype a lightweight token issuer and a proxy verifier for perf tests.
Eve (security): I'll write the crypto + compliance checklist.
Dan (runtime): one more: measure KV cache interactions when we burst validate — ensure we don't thundering herd the control-plane. consider leaky-bucket at proxy.
Alice M.: cool. let's sync tomorrow 10am. short meeting to lock defaults then roll RFC. :thumbsup:
